events.title: Treaty of Tordesillas Signed
events.description: Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, dividing newly discovered lands outside Europe along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. Spain received rights to lands west of the line and Portugal to lands east of it.
events.significance: The treaty shaped colonial claims in the Americas, Africa, and Asia, and explains why Portuguese is spoken in Brazil while Spanish dominates the rest of Latin America.

events.title: Lee Resolution Introduced in the Continental Congress
events.description: Richard Henry Lee of Virginia introduced a resolution to the Second Continental Congress declaring that the United Colonies are, and ought to be, free and independent states, and calling for foreign alliances and a plan of confederation.
events.significance: The resolution set in motion the drafting of the Declaration of Independence, which was adopted on July 4, 1776, and it was formally approved on July 2.

events.title: Gandhi's Pietermaritzburg Train Incident
events.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi, traveling in South Africa on a first-class ticket, was thrown off a train at Pietermaritzburg station for refusing to move to a third-class carriage reserved for non-whites.
events.significance: The incident is widely cited as a turning point that spurred Gandhi's commitment to resisting racial discrimination and led to the development of his philosophy of satyagraha.

events.title: Norway Dissolves Its Union with Sweden
events.description: The Norwegian Parliament (Storting) declared the union with Sweden dissolved, asserting Norway's independence after 91 years of union under a shared monarch.
events.significance: The declaration led to a plebiscite and the peaceful separation of the two nations, and Prince Carl of Denmark became King Haakon VII of Norway.

events.title: Death of Alan Turing
events.description: British mathematician and computer scientist Alan Turing died at age 41 at his home in Wilmslow, Cheshire, in what an inquest ruled a suicide by cyanide poisoning, following his 1952 conviction for homosexual acts.
events.significance: Turing's work on computability, the Turing machine, and wartime codebreaking at Bletchley Park laid the foundations of computer science and artificial intelligence; he was posthumously pardoned in 2013.
